130030.overview: Squash simulations are something of a rarity, and it was this niché that Krisalis aimed one of their many sports simulations into. The rules of squash are accurately recreated, with a realistic court layout (viewed isometrically) and a need to hit legal shots. Three different ball speeds, variable match lengths and an 'easy' mode are on offer. Different tournament types are on offer, at 'club' and 'tournament' levels, with a customisable ladder system of multiple divisions to rise up. There is a full roster of opponents to play in one-off or tournament modes.

130031.overview: "James Pond" is (obviously) a parody on the famous agent 007 stories. You control Pond, a fish-like creature, who has to complete several missions, while making his way through levels full of dangers and hostile creatures. It is not a typical "jump and run" game: instead of breezing through large levels, Pond has to complete unique missions for each game area: free hostages, detonate a structure, find keys, etc. It is possible to exit a level only after having completed the objective. Many missions are timed.

130032.overview:
In his second adventure James Pond must retrieve the toys Dr Maybe has stolen. Pond has been armed with an Inspector Gadget-style stretch device, which he can use to view higher areas or claw onto ceilings so as to slide across them.

The gameplay takes place across worlds themed around particular types of toys, such as sporting goods, candy and aircraft. The levels scroll sideways, although a small amount of vertical movement is included. On each level Pond must collect 2 penguins and reach the exit, although there are usually multiple exits and lots of secret areas to explore. After completing each pair of two worlds (each of which has three sub levels), a boss must be faced.

130033.overview:
Jet Fighter is a variant of Jetpac that is largely the same as the original game but features a larger play area and different types of enemies. The player controls an astronaut that first has to collect all three parts of his rocket and then fully fuel it so that it can take off. The rocket parts are located on various platforms that the astronaut has to use his jetpack to reach. After the rocket has been fully assembled fuel will start falling from the sky and once enough of it has been collected the rocket will automatically ascend.

The game is entirely played with the mouse, using one button to thrust upwards and the other to shoot at the strange beings that fly around. Any contact with these will lead to a lost life and the game ends on the third. There is also a time limit for each level. By shooting the beings points are earned and bonuses are earned by collecting falling objects.

480417.overview:
With the inauguration of the Thames Water Ring Main came the call for a licensed software program to teach students about its operation and water treatment process. Enter James Pond, codename Robocod, on license from Millennium Interactive. James and his friend Ronnie the Raindrop will swim underneath London together, illustrating the operation of the Ring Main through a series of basic action sequences. Following each individual section, James Pond will join the player in the classroom for a quick, multiple-choice lesson about the topic at hand.

The second game of the pack, Running Water, is a real-world simulation intended for older students.
